'''BTC & Crypto (BTCC)''' is a [[cryptocurrency exchange]] established in 2011. Incorporated in 2013 in [[Shanghai]], it became the largest cryptocurrency exchange by volume globally in November 2013. It ceased trading in China in 2017 due to regulatory changes by the Chinese government and was purchased in 2018 by an investment firm in Hong Kong.

== History ==

=== 2011–2017: Company beginnings ===
BTCC was founded by Bobby Lee, Yang Linke, and Huang Xiaoyu in 2011. Initially, it was a part-time project for Lee. BTCC (then known as BTC China) incorporated in 2013 and acquired investors, established a headquarters in [[Shanghai]], and had 20 employees. Lee became [[chief executive officer]]. Usage of BTCC increased following the elimination of trading fees and it became the largest [[Cryptocurrency exchange|bitcoin exchange]] by volume in the world in November 2013.<ref name="Forbes1">{{cite news |last1=Hill |first1=Kashmir |date=November 8, 2013 |title=From Walmart To Bitcoin: The CEO Behind The Chinese Exchange Sending BTC To New Highs |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/kashmirhill/2013/11/08/from-walmart-to-bitcoin-the-ceo-behind-the-chinese-exchange-sending-bitcoin-to-new-highs/ |accessdate=June 3, 2025 |work=Forbes}}</ref><ref name="WSJ1">{{cite news |last1=Chernova |first1=Yuliya |last2=Cheung |first2=Sonja |date=November 18, 2013 |title=Top Bitcoin Exchange BTC China Secures First VC Round |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/DJFVW00020131118e9bifc6wv |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20221212164544/https://www.wsj.com/amp/articles/DJFVW00020131118e9bifc6wv#selection-163.0-285.225 |archive-date=December 12, 2022 |accessdate=June 3, 2025 |work=The Wall Street Journal}}</ref><ref name="Wired1">{{cite magazine |last1=McMillan |first1=Robert |date=October 23, 2013 |title=This Chinese Exchange Just Pushed the Value of Bitcoins Over $200 |url=https://www.wired.com/2013/10/btc-china/ |accessdate=June 3, 2025 |magazine=Wired |archive-date=February 23, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250223154526/https://www.wired.com/2013/10/btc-china/ |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref> That month, BTCC received {{USD}}5 million in [[Series A]] funding from Lightspeed China Partners and [[Lightspeed Venture Partners]].<ref name="WSJ1" />

The company stopped accepting deposits of [[Yuan (currency)|yuan]] in December 2013 due to regulatory changes by the [[People's Bank of China]] that barred financial institutions from trading in bitcoin, leading third-party payment providers to end their service to BTCC.<ref name="Reuters1">{{cite news |last1=Rose |first1=Adam |date=December 18, 2013 |title=China tightens curbs on bitcoin trade |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/business/china-tightens-curbs-on-bitcoin-trade-idUSBRE9BH0HI/ |accessdate=June 3, 2025 |work=Reuters}}</ref> The company began taking yuan again in January 2014 after it further examined rules, which specifically barred banks from participating in bitcoin business activities.<ref name="WSJ2">{{cite news |last1=Casey |first1=Michael J. |date=January 31, 2014 |title=China Bitcoin Exchange Restores Deposit Facility |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052702303743604579353783803642644 |accessdate=June 3, 2025 |work=The Wall Street Journal}}</ref> It rebranded in 2015, changing its name to BTCC.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Biggs |first1=John |date=September 15, 2015 |title=BTCChina Rebrands to BTCC |url=https://techcrunch.com/2015/09/15/btcchina-rebrands-to-btcc/ |access-date=June 9, 2025 |work=TechCrunch}}</ref>

===2017–present: Growth and international expansion===
BTCC stopped all trading in China in September 2017 following an announcement by the People's Bank that the country would ban [[initial coin offering]]s.<ref name="CNN1">{{cite news |title=China's bitcoin crackdown forces exchanges to close. The price is crashing |last1=Iyengar |first1=Rishi |url=https://money.cnn.com/2017/09/15/technology/china-bitcoin-exchanges-prices-crash/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170915133707/http://money.cnn.com/2017/09/15/technology/china-bitcoin-exchanges-prices-crash/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 15, 2017 |work=CNN |date=September 15, 2017 |accessdate=June 3, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=It's only a matter of time before China lifts crypto exchange ban, entrepreneur says |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2018/01/03/china-to-eventually-lift-cryptocurrency-bitcoin-exchange-ban-bobby-lee-btcc.html |work=CNBC |date=January 3, 2018 |access-date=June 9, 2025 |last1=Murphy |first1=Dan}}</ref> The company was purchased by an unnamed firm in [[Hong Kong]] in January 2018. Portions of its services were registered in the United Kingdom.<ref name="BI1">{{cite news |title=An unnamed Hong Kong-based blockchain investment fund has acquired Chinese crypto exchange BTCC |last1=Nonninger |first1=Lea |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/unnamed-hong-kong-based-blockchain-investment-fund-acquired-chinese-crypto-exchange-btcc-2018-1 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180221112432/https://www.businessinsider.com/unnamed-hong-kong-based-blockchain-investment-fund-acquired-chinese-crypto-exchange-btcc-2018-1 |archive-date=February 21, 2018 |work=Business Insider |date=January 31, 2018 |accessdate=June 3, 2025}}</ref>

BTCC was among 16 foreign cryptocurrency businesses lacking the proper registration to operate in South Korea in 2022. An intelligence unit of the [[Financial Services Commission (South Korea)|Financial Services Commission]] reported the businesses to the nation's investigative body and asked other agencies to block access to the firms' local websites.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kim |first1=Hooyeon |title=South Korea to Block Foreign Crypto Exchanges Lacking Permit |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-08-18/s-korea-steps-up-scrutiny-of-unregistered-foreign-crypto-firms |work=Bloomberg News  |access-date=September 3, 2025 |date= August 17, 2022}}</ref> 

Dan Liu became CEO of BTCC in May 2025.<ref>{{cite web |title=BTCC Exchange Appoints Dan Liu as CEO Ahead of 14th Anniversary Milestone |website=BTCC |date=May 21, 2025 |access-date=June 3, 2025 |url=https://www.btcc.com/en-US/btcc-updates/company-news/btcc-exchange-appoints-dan-liu-as-ceo-ahead-of-14th-anniversary-milestone?utm_source=branding&utm_medium=EN-DanLiu}}</ref> The same year, the company made [[Jaren Jackson Jr.]] a [[brand ambassador]].<ref> {{cite news |title=Grizzlies star becomes global brand ambassador for crypto exchange |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/memphis/news/2025/08/15/jaren-jackson-jr-btcc-crypto-ambassador-grizzlies.html |last1=Yusuf |first1=Omer |date=August 15, 2025 |work=Memphis Business Journal |access-date=September 3, 2025}} </ref>
